description: ProcessManager.stopAll uses Promise.all instead of Promise.allSettled. The plan explicitly requires allSettled 'so one hang does not block others'. With Promise.all, a single stop rejection (e.g., a tree-kill failure on Windows that is not the ESRCH wildcard) propagates out of stopAll, is caught by index.ts shutdown, logs the error, and proceeds to server.close() and process.exit(0) — but the remaining managed children never get killed because their stop promises were not awaited. This breaks the no-orphan acceptance criterion under partial failure.
suggestedFix: Replace Promise.all with Promise.allSettled in stopAll; collect rejections into a returned errors array or write them to stderr inside the helper so the caller can still log them without short-circuiting the rest of the shutdown sweep.
